_note: Group E (2026-10-01): what the player can carry and wear. Design and Yannick's answers: docs/CREATION_AND_GEAR.md section 4. Six slots; two numbers on armour - protection (taken off every blow received, never below one) and heavy (two heavy pieces or more cost one tile of movement a turn); weapons keep content/duel.json's numbers. Each item names how it is drawn: a layer of view3d/layers/ in a slot of PaperDoll.ORDER, with an optional recolouring in the recipes' terms (hue, saturation scale, saturation floor, value scale). Items are unique: a second of the same is nothing more.
_draw_note: E4: an item drawn by a piece of tools/draw_cast_looks.gd - the same pieces group L's looks wear - is baked by tools/draw_player_layers.gd into the layers it names: his figure is dressed in it, and what changed is the item's layer; what the piece took away (a helm's hiding of hair and ears) is its mask.
_slots_note: The hands are two slots, not one with gloves (Yannick, 2026-10-01): the fight's two ways to strike and its U key stay as the tutorial teaches them; a glove is three pixels on screen.

empty._note: What shows in a slot nothing fills: the linen he wears under everything, and bare feet. Not items - nothing to carry, nothing to take off.

cloth_tunic._why: What he wakes in, in the colour chosen at creation.

short_sword._why: Lies on a grave just past the fairy (Yannick, 2026-10-01): at the belt walking, in the hand fighting.

hunting_bow._why: Wren's spare, handed over as the bow lesson begins - the fact that gave it since T5 is now the item. On the back (bow_on_back, since the review of group E: it walked in his hand), and in the hand when it is the weapon in use.

leather_cap._why: The works' guards wear it (group L); a beaten one leaves it.

royal_helm._why: The king's guards' closed helm, by a miracle.

royal_breastplate._own_colour: Yannick, 2026-10-01: in the king's set the player looked exactly like a king's guard. His surcoat is his own - painted in his tunic's blue, without the crown, and moved to the colour chosen at creation like his tunic; the iron keeps its paint (PaperDoll.KEEPS_PAINT).

_start_note: No weapon: the first sword is picked up by the graves.
_bare_hands_note: A player with nothing in the weapon slot strikes with his fists: content/duel.json's fists_damage, weaker than the sword's, so a player who walked past the sword is weaker, not stuck.

loot._note: What a beaten fighter leaves: what you saw on him, keyed by his kind or else his trade (the gatekeeper wears the works' guards' look). A king's guard leaves one piece each, by his seat in the fight: the first the helm, the second the breastplate, the third the leggings. Taken in a fight, it goes into the bag, and on once the fight is over where its slot is free.
